title: Computability theory: standard extensions and remaining specialist boundaries
area_fit: The current development supplies ordinary and relative computation, finite injury, splitting, effective trees and low basis. The selected standard extensions connect explicit growth examples, uniform inseparability, stronger reductions, tree-path degrees, domination, finite-extension genericity and enumeration without repetition. These extend existing themes without assuming randomness, measure theory or higher recursion theory.
reading_order_rule: Place Ackermann after universal computation and Busy Beaver after the jump for its function-oracle comparison. Effective inseparability follows uniform self-reference. Stronger reductions follow the existing incomparable-degree entry so its actual finite-prefix certificate interfaces are available; domination, 1-genericity and jump inversion then precede finite injury. Friedberg numberings follow Rogers isomorphism. PA degrees follow the existing low-basis entry; hyperimmune-free basis follows PA degrees and uses the earlier domination entry.
coverage_boundary: Density, minimal degrees, highness characterizations, randomness, algorithmic information, hyperarithmetic theory and reverse mathematics remain later specialist development. Alternative lambda-calculus models and standard word, tiling and Post correspondence applications are separate branches. Effective model theory needs a cross-area interface plan. Resource complexity belongs in a separate area; Hilbert’s tenth problem needs substantial number theory.
execution_and_ownership: Future entry creation uses prompts01–06: root selects concrete scopes and source support before delegating entry pipelines, maintains reading order and shared integration, and coordinates independent reviews and writing builds.
source_limits: Exact supporting passages for all ten selected standard scopes have now been inspected at the root. The permanent source register records the checked versions, selected proofs, exercise-only leads, excluded adjacent arguments and checked repairs. Corpus-specific effective implementations remain explicit proof obligations; no whole-publication audit is claimed.
